_readme: Extra phrases that should make the desk treat a message as a crisis.
WHO THIS FILE IS FOR: a native Nepali speaker, ideally alongside someone
with clinical training. The built-in list in adapt/crisis.py was written
English-first, and every gap found in review was a Nepali or an indirect
form. This file is where that gets corrected, without a deploy.
HOW TO EDIT: entries are plain phrases, not regular expressions. Type the
words as a member would type them. Spacing between words is flexible and
matching ignores case, so 'बाँच्न मन छैन' also matches 'बाँच्न  मन  छैन'.
You cannot break the matcher with a stray bracket; a phrase that fails to
compile is ignored and the built-in list still runs.
'phrases' matches the whole phrase. Use it for things said outright.
'pairs' matches a stem near any one of its markers, within about 40
characters. Use it when Nepali inflection would otherwise need a dozen
separate phrases: the stem 'बाँच' covers बाँच्न, बाँच्नु, बाँच्ने and
बाँचिरहन all at once.
THIS FILE CAN ONLY WIDEN THE NET, NEVER NARROW IT. That is deliberate. A
wrong match costs a member one gentle message they did not need. A missed
match sends the message to retrieval, which is well tuned on financial
content and will answer despair about a loan with repayment penalties.
Removing a pattern stays a code change, with a test.
DO NOT put helpline numbers here. Those live in crisis_resources.json and
must be confirmed against a current official source before they are shown.
